newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Andina says workers ended strike.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Andina says workers ended strike.

text.p: Striking workers at Chile's main Coca-Cola bottler, Embotelladora Andina SA, have accepted a company pay offer and returned to work, the company said on Friday.
Representatives of the two striking unions accepted the company's last contract offer, which had been made before the five-day walkout began, Andina said in a statement to the Stocks Superintendency.
"The strike has concluded and all workers have returned to their jobs," the statement read.
The two unions, accounting for 645 of Andina's 1,000-odd workers, went on strike on Monday after contract talks broke down. Union officials could not be reached for comment Friday.
Workers at a much-smaller Coca-Cola bottler, Embotelladora Arica, in the city of Arica on the border with Peru, have been on strike since last Saturday. The company is not affiliated to Andina.
